claim: The AMERICAN CONGRESS reverse legend on the 1787 Fugio cent is Newman 1-CC pattern only; normal circulation issues use UNITED STATES or STATES UNITED.

topic: Fugio New Haven Restrike Attributed to Rust
claim: The so-called New Haven Restrike of the Fugio cent was struck around 1860 by Horatio N. Rust from copy dies following C. Wyllys Betts die discovery and is not 1787 circulation.
Abel Buell engraved the dies for the 1787 Fugio coppers struck in New Haven Connecticut.

topic: Fugio Mintage Estimated Treasury Weight Count
claim: Fugio cent mintage is estimated at ~398,577 pieces based on Treasury weight-count delivery records of 8,968 pounds of copper.
Rank 0 image parity targets require obverse sundial and reverse 13 linked chain rings with WE ARE ONE for primary presentation.
The Grand Watermelon banknote is the Series 1890 $1000 Treasury Note (Coin Note) Fr. 379a/379b, not a Gold Certificate.
The 1923 $5 Porthole note depicting Abraham Lincoln is a Silver Certificate (Fr. 282), not a Legal Tender note.
The vignette on the Series 1899 $5 Silver Certificate depicts Chief Running Antelope of the Oncpapa Sioux, not Chief Black Hawk.
William Wood Hibernia coppers and 1767 French colonies sou coppers marked RF circulated as token copper currency in colonial America.

topic: Federal Reserve Bank Notes vs FRNs
claim: Federal Reserve Bank Notes (FRBN) of 1915 and 1918 National Currency series are obligations of individual Federal Reserve Banks, distinct from Federal Reserve Notes.
U.S. classic gold coin denominations are $2.50 Quarter Eagle, $5 Half Eagle, $10 Eagle, and $20 Double Eagle.
U.S.-Philippines 20 Centavos and 50 Centavos silver coins were struck in .900 fineness from 1903 to 1906, and reduced to .750 fineness in 1907.
The Manila Mint struck coins with the 'M' mint mark beginning in 1925; although opened in 1920, issues from 1920 to 1922 did not carry the M mintmark.
Filipino artist and master engraver Melecio Figueroa (spelled Melecio, not Melicio) designed the US-Philippines coinage obverse and reverse devices.
1793 Half Cent dies were engraved by Henry Voigt and Joseph Wright; 1,758 Flowing Hair silver dollars were delivered in October 1794.
The official U.S. Mint mintage for the 1921-S Walking Liberty Half Dollar is exactly 548,000 pieces.

The U.S. Mint Annual Report records 2,876,381 Philadelphia half dollars manufactured in calendar year 1955 (total includes proof coins); the catalog business-strike figure 2,498,181 is a Tier-B numismatic convention (subtracting 378,200 proofs) not printed in the Mint Annual Report.

The Walking Liberty half dollar mintmark was relocated from the obverse to the reverse by Mint administrative order on February 14, 1917; 1917-D and 1917-S coins exist with obverse and reverse mintmarks.

topic: A6 Proof and Mint Set Packaging Parity
claim: Modern U.S. Mint uncirculated mint sets and proof sets packaging documentation maintains full parity across envelope and plastic lens specifications.

topic: National Medals and Assay Commission Catalog
